source: Realtor.com lock-in report, Nov. 2026, via BAM

headline: Moving now costs
*$1,100 more a month*
slides.fig_caption: Monthly payment jump if a typical owner buys a median home
slides.sub: New Realtor.com research shows why so many owners still won't list.

slides.label: of households can afford the median home at *7.32%*
slides.body: That home runs $2,468 a month in principal and interest, vs. $1,332 for the typical current owner at a median rate near 4%.

slides.title: Payment jump to buy a *median home*
slides.note: In about *a third of the 100 largest metros*, buying would more than double the typical owner's payment.

slides.title: Rates alone *won't close it*
points: At 6%, a median-priced home runs $2,154 a month, still 61.7% above what owners pay today.
At 5%, the payment falls to $1,929, and 54.8% of households could afford it, up from 44.5% now.
Realtor.com's December 2025 read put the jump at 73.2%. This update puts it at 85.3%.

slides.title: Sell the *move*, not the rate
slides.body: Waiting for 6% won't erase the gap for most owners. The listings that do come will go to agents who can walk sellers through the full math: equity, the next payment and why they want to move.
